scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “Equidistribution of primitive quartic torus packets for arbitrary orders” (preprints/Equidistribution-of-Primitive-Quartic-Torus-Packets-for-Arbitrary-Orders-October-5-2026/quartic-torus-packets.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 015 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 95c2a937da74097a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (Ki, Oi, σi) be any sequence in which Ki is a primitive totally real quartic field, Oi is an order in Ki, and σi is an ordering of its real embeddings. If | Disc(Oi)| → ∞, then Z X4 f dµOi,σi −→ Z X4 f dm4 for every f ∈ Cc(X4). There is no escape of mass: for every ε > 0 there is a compact K ⊂ X4 such that µOi,σi (K) ≥ 1 − ε for all sufficiently large i.
